nodes.norm_label: passphrase stored in macos keychain, not the workspace
nodes.rationale: Key passphrases are secrets; keeping them in the OS keychain keeps them out of workspace files that may be exported or shared. Private keys are read only when a request needs them.

nodes.label: Export variable values: Blank by default, Keep with warning
nodes.norm_label: export variable values: blank by default, keep with warning
nodes.rationale: Variable values can hold tokens and passwords, so exports keep names but empty values unless the user explicitly chooses Keep, which shows a sharing warning. gRPC calls are dropped (with a warning) for Postman v2.1 and HAR, which cannot represent them.

nodes.label: HAR import secret stripping (Cookie/Authorization/Set-Cookie removed, hosts as variables)
nodes.norm_label: har import secret stripping (cookie/authorization/set-cookie removed, hosts as variables)
nodes.rationale: Captured browser traffic carries live session credentials; stripping them by default and replacing hosts with {{baseUrl}}/{{authUrl}} keeps imported collections shareable.

nodes.label: 'Changed on the way in' lossy-conversion report
nodes.norm_label: 'changed on the way in' lossy-conversion report
nodes.rationale: Import surfaces every lossy mapping (OAuth2 -> Bearer {{token}} because voidHTTP has no OAuth2 flow yet, webhooks/callbacks dropped, bodies synthesized from schema) so the user is never silently given a different collection. Nothing is saved until Import is pressed.

nodes.rationale: Hero with rippling icon orbit, tagline 'Antisocial by design. Speaks API, avoids people.', copyable version chip, GitHub / license / issue links.

nodes.rationale: Allow use/modify/fork/redistribute; deny selling, paid hosting or support; keep NOTICE and link back.

nodes.norm_label: dev build channel tag (title strip pill)
nodes.rationale: Dev and local builds say what they are (DEV + short sha, git-describe version like v0.1.6-12-g8b686a8+); official releases show nothing new. Clicking the pill opens About.

nodes.label: CONNECT / CONNACK connection view
nodes.rationale: Shows what was sent vs what broker granted (e.g. server keep alive lowered 60s to 30s); refused login card for CONNACK 0x86 links to Auth and environment variables.

nodes.label: MQTT message stream with broker acks
nodes.norm_label: mqtt message stream with broker acks
nodes.rationale: Each publish shows the broker's answer under it: QoS 1 PUBACK, QoS 2 PUBREC to PUBCOMP, QoS 0 'no ack'. Received messages expand to topic, matched filter, retained flag, properties.

nodes.label: MQTT 5 publish properties
nodes.rationale: Content type, payload format, response topic, correlation data, message expiry and user properties sit behind a Payload|Properties seg so the payload keeps the room; hidden for MQTT 3.1.1.

nodes.label: MQTT request editor (Message / Topics / Auth / Last Will / Settings)
nodes.norm_label: mqtt request editor (message / topics / auth / last will / settings)
nodes.rationale: MQTT lives in the same method menu and collections as HTTP/Kafka/WS; Connect/Disconnect replaces Send, method and broker URL lock while connected.

nodes.label: MQTT connection settings (version, client ID, clean start, session expiry, keep alive)
nodes.norm_label: mqtt connection settings (version, client id, clean start, session expiry, keep alive)
nodes.rationale: Empty client ID = random voidhttp+10 hex per Connect, because two clients with one ID kick each other off. Not built: MQTT 3.1, topic aliases, MQTT 5 enhanced auth.

nodes.label: MQTT topic subscription list
nodes.rationale: Changes apply at once while connected (on = SUBSCRIBE, off/removed = UNSUBSCRIBE); shows granted QoS vs asked and reason codes like 0x87 Not authorized; supports + / # wildcards, $share groups, MQTT 5 options (No local, Retain as published, Retained messages).

nodes.label: Title-strip update chip (Update / Updating % / Restart to update / Update failed)
nodes.norm_label: title-strip update chip (update / updating % / restart to update / update failed)

nodes.label: Update popover per step (release notes, downloading, ready, failed)
nodes.norm_label: update popover per step (release notes, downloading, ready, failed)
nodes.rationale: User keeps working while downloading; failure keeps the current version unchanged and offers Download from GitHub plus Try again.

nodes.label: HTTP-response card metaphor for About sections
nodes.norm_label: http-response card metaphor for about sections
nodes.rationale: Each About section is styled as a request line with status: GET /releases/latest 304 Not Modified (up to date), 200 OK (update), 206 Partial Content (downloading), 205 Reset Content (restart), GET /license 200 OK.

nodes.label: Updates disabled in dev builds
nodes.rationale: Check automatically is off and disabled in dev builds so an update never replaces the dev build; a 'Get the release' link is offered instead.

nodes.label: Transport and TLS derived from broker URL scheme
nodes.norm_label: transport and tls derived from broker url scheme
nodes.rationale: mqtt:// TCP, mqtts:// TCP+TLS, ws:// WebSocket, wss:// WebSocket+TLS; no separate TLS toggle. CA/client certs (mTLS, AWS IoT Core) come from Settings > Certificates.

nodes.label: Void / Black-Hole Brand Motif
nodes.rationale: Concentric darkening circles (#1a3f9a to #050f2b) inside a glass ring on a blue gradient tile, crossed by a white diagonal slash, read as a void / null-set symbol that names the product voidHTTP.

nodes.label: Graphify Graph-First Agent Workflow
nodes.rationale: Agents read graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md first and treat only EXTRACTED edges as facts; INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS edges need confirmation.

nodes.label: Local-First: No Account, Cloud or Telemetry
nodes.norm_label: local-first: no account, cloud or telemetry
nodes.rationale: Data is plain JSON on disk so users can back up, grep and commit it; only self-initiated network call is the update check.

nodes.label: Never on the Wishlist (no accounts, cloud sync, co-editing)
nodes.norm_label: never on the wishlist (no accounts, cloud sync, co-editing)
nodes.rationale: An API client that wants you on a team plan is what voidHTTP was built to escape; collaboration happens via Git and OpenAPI files in repos.

nodes.label: Requests Run in Rust (reqwest + rustls)
nodes.rationale: No CORS issues, pooled connections, and the UI never freezes while waiting on slow servers.

nodes.label: Dev Build Tag (DEV <commit> pill)
nodes.rationale: Dev builds show branch/git describe and disable update checks so a dev build is never mistaken for, or replaced by, the GitHub release.

nodes.norm_label: security in-scope areas (imports, responses, secrets, tls/network, updates)

nodes.label: Release Process (tag push, release.yml, draft release)
nodes.norm_label: release process (tag push, release.yml, draft release)
nodes.rationale: Draft is published by hand so /releases/latest keeps pointing at the previous release and nobody gets a half-baked update.

nodes.norm_label: certs.rs (single rustls clientconfig, custom cas, mtls)

nodes.label: HTTP Request Flow (prepare, send_request, show and keep)
nodes.norm_label: http request flow (prepare, send_request, show and keep)
nodes.rationale: Address-bar preview reuses prepare() with a size budget so expanding variables cannot freeze the UI; clients pooled per redirect/TLS-skip/client-cert combination.

nodes.norm_label: kafka.rs engine (rskafka wire protocol, own connections, murmur2)

nodes.norm_label: mqtt.rs engine (own mqtt packet code, qos flows, subscription diff)

nodes.norm_label: net.rs (dns / doh via hickory, socks5/http proxy, net_test)
nodes.rationale: Every engine connects through net.rs and certs.rs so Settings apply to every kind of request.

nodes.label: Kafka Support (no consumer group)
nodes.rationale: Reads partitions from leaders without a consumer group and never commits offsets, so other services keep every record and no rebalance is triggered.

nodes.norm_label: network settings (secure dns / doh, proxy, connection check)
